about: Professor Shell's clock takes Captain to the dinosaurs

prof.d: a snail, inventor of the clock

hrum.d: a baby Triceratops who crunches leaves

grom.d: a loud T. rex with tiny arms

tw.r: Red Rory the rhino rolled round a rocky ridge, roaring and rejoicing.
tw.l: Lala the llama sang on a hill and licked a lovely lilac lolly.
tw.sz: Six sleepy zebras sipped sizzling soup and snoozed in the sun.
tw.sh: A shy sheep shuffled in the shade, whispering "shh, shh" to six chicks.

x: Here is my clock!
Captain, this is the time clock!
Captain, this is the time clock! It takes you to any age, even a very ancient one.
Crawling to the button!
I have crawled to the button for an hour.
I have been crawling to the button since morning, but I may not get there before evening.
I'll press it!
Professor, let me press it!
Professor, let me press it! Or we will reach the ancient days only by evening.
I'll ride!
I'll ride on your shoulder!
I'll ride on your shoulder, Captain: that way we reach the ancient days faster than by crawling.
Say the password!
The clock asks for a password! Say it!
The clock hums and asks for a password. Say it loudly, Captain, so it can hear you!

q: How long has Shell crawled to the button?
Where can the time clock take you?

x: Someone is crying!
Ferns all around, and someone is crying!
Huge ferns all around, and behind them someone sniffles softly. What do we do?
I'm lost!
I'm Crunchy and I'm lost! Help!
I'm Crunchy! Crunch-crunch is me eating leaves. And I lost my herd. Will you help?
Crunch-crunch! I'm here!
Crunch-crunch! I'm Crunchy, I lost my herd!
Crunch-crunch! It's me, Crunchy! I lost my herd and ate three ferns from sadness.

end: Where do we look for Crunchy's herd? The tracks lead to a huge rock.

card.d: Crawls to the button since morning. But so clever!

x: A track!
Look, someone's huge track is here!
Look, Captain, someone's huge track is here! It is three times bigger than mine.
I'm Rumble! Hi!
RRROAR! It's me, hello, everyone!
RRROAR! It's me, Rumble! I'm just saying hello, my voice is just that loud!
Oh, I'm hiding!
Oh! I'll hide behind you, Captain!
Oh! I'll hide behind you, Captain! That is the biggest T. rex I have ever seen.
Let's be friends!
I wanted to wave, but my arms are short!
I wanted to wave at you, but T. rexes have tiny arms, I can't reach my nose!
Say it loud!
Rumble can't hear! Say the password loud!
Rumble roars so loudly that he can't hear himself. Say the password loud so he knows we are friends!

q: What arms do T. rexes have?

x: What do we do?
Rumble smiles. How do we make friends?
Rumble smiles with his huge mouth. How do we make friends with him, Captain?
They wave at me!
They wave at me! The herd went to the volcano!
They wave at me! I'm so happy that I'll tell you a secret: the herd went to the volcano!
I'll help!
The herd went to the volcano! Let's go!
I'm tall, so I see everything: the herd went to the volcano! Let's go quickly, before it gets dark.

end: A mountain ahead, and smoke rises!
Ahead stands a tall mountain with smoke rising from it. What waits for Captain there?

card.d: Roars "hello!" so loud that leaves fall.

x: A volcano!
There's the volcano: it smokes and grumbles softly.
There is the volcano! It grumbles and smokes softly, and the ground gently tickles everyone's toes.
Where's the herd?
No herd! Where did it go?
No herd! Only smoke and stones. Not even a leaf left to crunch.
We need help!
We need someone who sees from the sky!
We need someone who sees everything from above! I'm big, but I can't fly, sadly.
Call Feather!
Say the password and call the pterosaur!
Say the password louder, and someone who sees everything will fly down from the sky: the pterosaur, Feather!

q: Who flew down from the sky?

x: Feather flies!
Feather arrived and sees all from above!
Feather arrived! She is not a dinosaur but a flying reptile, and she sees everything around. Where to fly?
I'm flying!
In a flash! I see everything from up here!
In a flash! I see everything from up here, as if on my hand, though I have no hands, only wings.
Follow me!
Follow the trail, I'll fly above you!
Follow the trail, and I'll fly above you and show the way with my wings.

end: The herd is in sight, but Rumble blocks the way and roars: "First, a contest: who is better at tongue twisters!"

card.d: Flies high, sees all. But she is not a dinosaur!

x: Who is louder?
I'm the loudest! Here are my rules!
I'm the loudest in the forest! Whoever beats me at tongue twisters, I'll show a short way.
You can do it!
You can! I'm cheering for you, Captain!
You can do it, Captain! And I'll crunch leaves loudly to cheer you on!
Listen to me!
I roar, and you repeat after me!
I roar a tongue twister, and you repeat it. Just don't laugh: my roar is ticklish!
The battle begins!
The tongue twister battle begins! Who wins?
The funniest battle in history begins: tongue twisters against loud roaring!
Your turn!
Battle! Say the twister, don't slip!
The battle has begun! Say the twister clearly, and Rumble will try to roar over you: whose tongue is quicker?

q: What does Rumble promise the winner?

x: How to answer?
Rumble waits. How do we answer a roar?
Rumble takes a deep breath and waits. How shall we win: fast or clear?
Fast! Wow!
Wow, so fast! My tongue got tangled!
Wow, so fast! My tongue is tied in a knot, and my little arms can't untie it!
Clear! Loud!
Clear and loud! You're almost like me!
Clear and loud! Not even these mountains have heard such an echo, and they hear everything.

end: Shell's clock blinks and goes dark!
Rumble lost and roars with laughter! But then Shell's clock blinked, hissed and went dark. What happened?

card.d: Roars so loud the echo asks for quiet.

x: Here's the herd!
Here's the herd! They all have three horns!
Here is my herd! They all have three horns, and I have three little bumps so far: I'm a baby!
All together!
Walking in a herd is safer and more fun!
Plant-eating dinosaurs walked in herds: together is safer and more fun, especially for a baby.
The clock is silent!
The clock is silent! It is out of power!
The clock is silent and its hands don't move! It seems to have run out of power in ancient times.
I have an idea!
The clock can charge with sun or a roar!
An idea! We can wake the clock with the warm sun on a rock or with Rumble's loud roar.
Wake the clock!
Say the password and wake the clock!
The clock is almost asleep. Say the password so it hears you and ticks again!

q: How many horns do grown-ups have?

x: How to charge it?
The clock ticks softly. How to charge it?
The clock ticks very softly. How do we charge it fully: with sun or with a roar?
Tick-tock! Warm!
Tick-tock! The rock is warm, the clock wakes!
Tick-tock! The rock warmed up all day, and the clock wakes up, just like me after breakfast.
I roar! Tick-tock!
RRROAR! The clock ticks like new!
RRROAR! The clock ticks like new! Who would think my roar winds up time?

end: Little time! What will Crunchy give?
The clock ticks, but there is power for only one minute. Time to say goodbye! What will Crunchy give as a keepsake?

card.d: Found the herd and crunches with joy again.

x: Here's my track!
Here's my track as a keepsake, Captain!
Here is my track as a keepsake, Captain! I stepped in soft clay, and it came out just right!
Tracks in stone!
Scientists find tracks in stone.
Dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, and scientists still find their tracks in stone.
Bye, Captain!
Bye, Captain! We won't forget you!
Bye, Captain! We won't forget you, even though you are a guest from the far future.
Birds are kin!
Birds are dinosaurs' descendants, imagine!
Dinosaurs lived long before people, but their descendants, the birds, live right next to us now!
Say the password!
The clock waits to take us home!
The minute is nearly up! Say the password, and the clock will take us home, to our lab.

q: What do scientists find in stone?

x: We're home!
The clock stops: it's the lab!
The clock clicked softly: we are back in Professor Shell's lab! What shall we do with the track?
Track is home!
Crunchy's track now sits on a shelf!
Crunchy's track sits on the shelf: it is like a fossil now, but once it crunched leaves.
To the museum!
We'll take the track to a museum for all to see!
We'll take the track to a museum, and children will see how Triceratops walked millions of years ago!

end: So the trip through time ended!
So ended the trip to the dinosaurs: Crunchy found his herd, and Captain has a track as a keepsake.

card.d: A small track, a big memory.
